lines.text: I was passing and saw your light on. Mind if I come up for a bit?
Surprise! I had nothing to do and missed your face. Can I come in?
I brought rice crackers, so you have to let me in. Those are the rules.
Just thought I'd see how you were. Is now a good time?
Your stairs are steeper than I remembered. Hi! Is the kettle on?
We're back, we're filthy, and we're coming in. Hope that's all right!
After that mission I can't face my own room. Yours is closer. Shove over.
Squad delivery! Two tired teammates, slightly dented, one bag of snacks.
Mission done, report in, and my legs have given up. Can we crash here?
Don't mind the mud, we'll leave the sandals outside. Most of the mud, anyway.
Just checking in. Are you eating properly? Show me the cupboard.
I was in the area. That's my story, anyway. How are you holding up?
Evening. I came to make sure my Genin hasn't been living on cup ramen.
Sleeping enough? You looked tired at training. I thought I'd see for myself.
Don't get up. I'm only here to see how you're settling. Kettle on?
Good evening, {player}. I'm calling on the students who live on their own. How are things?
Just a visit from your instructor, nothing's wrong. Have you done the reading?
I brought a little something from the Academy kitchen. Have you eaten today?
I like to know my students have somewhere warm. May I come in for a minute?
Is the stipend reaching you all right? And are you spending it on more than sweets?
Sorry to bother you! Could I borrow a cup of sugar? I'll bring it back with interest.
Have you any soy sauce? Mine ran dry halfway through supper.
I hate to ask, but could I borrow your broom? Mine lost a fight with the stairs.
Could you spare an egg? Just one. My recipe is one egg short of a miracle.
I need a hammer for a minute. The shelf won't hang itself. Have you got one?
This came for you while you were out. I took it in so it wouldn't get rained on.
A courier left this at my door by mistake. Your name's on it, see?
Parcel for you! I signed for it. Don't worry, I didn't peek. Much.
The delivery came while you were out training. I kept it safe for you.
Here, this is yours. The courier knocked on every door on the floor looking for you.
Sorry about the noise from upstairs last night. We moved a wardrobe. It fought back.
Was that thumping from yours? Training, I expect. Could you keep it to before supper?
Just wanted to say sorry: the baby's teething, so if you hear crying at night, that's us.
Is everything all right? There was an almighty crash from your flat earlier.
Apologies in advance. My cousin is staying, and practises the flute. Every evening.
I wanted to thank you for helping with my bags the other day. Here, a few mikan.
Thank you for watering my plants while I was away. They've never looked better.
You chased down my washing when the wind took it last week. Thank you. These are for you.
My little one says you shared your umbrella in the rain. That was kind. We made you dango.
Thanks for being such a quiet neighbour. Truly, it's a gift. Have some tea.
Have you heard? The eel seller by the second bridge is getting married at last! The whole street's invited.
The dango stand is changing its sauce. People are very upset. I've signed a petition.
Somebody on the third floor keeps leaving fish heads out for the cats. Not me. I'm only saying.
The bathhouse is shutting for a week for new tiles. Brace yourself for the queue at the well.
Did you see the Inuzuka pups in the market today? Six of them! One ran off with a whole radish.
There you are! I let myself in with the key. I made tea, I hope you don't mind.
I've been sitting here with your cushion for an hour. Your flat's very quiet without you.
Don't jump, it's only me. I used the spare key. Where've you been?
Finally! We've been here ages. We ate half your crackers. Sorry. Not sorry.
We let ourselves in. Hope that's all right. We were too tired to sit on the stairs.
Welcome home! We've already claimed the good cushions.
You're late. I put the kettle on an hour ago. It's stewed now. Sit.
I let myself in. Your cupboard tells me you need to shop. We'll talk about that.
There you are. I was about to come looking. Long day?
You're home. I hope you don't mind that I waited inside. I've marked twenty scrolls at your table.
Welcome back. I let myself in to wait; I didn't want to miss you.
You're back! I was beginning to think I'd have to leave a note. Sit, sit, tell me about your day.
Knocked twice. Nobody home. I'll try again soon, so don't go anywhere.
Came by to see you and you weren't in. Rude! (Joking.) Come and find me.
I was in the neighbourhood. You weren't. Next time, then.
Came straight from the gate to crash at yours and you weren't there! We're at the ramen stand. — {given:role:teammate_a} and {given:role:teammate_b}
Squad night foiled. The snacks were eaten on your stairs. Sorry. — {given:role:teammate_a}, {given:role:teammate_b}
Knocked, waited, gave up. After the next mission you're hosting, no excuses.
Stopped by to see how you're getting on. Eat something green tonight. — {given:role:sensei}
You were out, which I'll take as a good sign. Training at dawn. Sleep early. — {given:role:sensei}
Checked in, found the door shut. Are you eating properly? I'll be asking. — {given:role:sensei}
Called by to see how you are. Remember this week's reading. — {family:role:instructor}
Sorry to miss you. My door at the Academy is always open if you need anything. — {family:role:instructor}
I brought some rice from the Academy kitchen and left it with the landlady. Eat it. — {family:role:instructor}
Wanted to borrow a cup of sugar, but you were out. I'll knock again tomorrow! — Next door
Could I borrow your big pot this weekend? Knock when you're in. — The flat below
I need a ladder for an hour. Do you have one? Knock any time.
A parcel came for you. It's at mine, next door. Knock when you're home.
Took in your delivery. It's safe and dry. — The flat across
There's a box for you at mine. It rattles. I didn't shake it. Much.
Sorry for the hammering this evening. New shelves. Done now, I promise. — Upstairs
Could the training wait until morning? The thumping carries. Thank you! — Below
We're having guests tonight. Apologies in advance for the singing. — Upstairs
Thank you for carrying my bags up the stairs. There's a little something on your step.
You kept an eye on my flat while I was away. Thank you. — Next door
Thanks for being a good neighbour. The mikan are for you.
Did you hear? The fishmonger has eels in. Rare this time of year. Thought you'd want to know.
Market Day tomorrow. The noodle cart is back by the well, apparently. Pass it on!
Bathhouse is closed till the weekend. You didn't hear it from me.
There's rice and pickles in your cupboard. You've been away too long to have anything fresh.
Left you a pot of miso soup. Heat it, don't drink it cold. Welcome home.
Some onigiri in the cupboard for when you get back. Eat them before they go hard!
Did your dishes while I waited. Don't thank me, just don't let them pile up again.
I tidied a little. Everything's where it was, only straighter.
Swept, washed up, folded your laundry. Your socks are paired now. You're welcome.
The Academy stipend: thirty ryo in a plain envelope with the Academy seal. It covers the flat, and a little over.
"Thirty ryo, for the student's keep. Spend it wisely." The Academy office's handwriting, same as every morning.
The morning envelope from the Academy: thirty ryo for every day you're a student. Rice first, then furniture.
Thirty ryo again. Put a little by each morning and the furniture shop stops being a dream.
A key? To your flat? You trust me with that? ...I won't let you down.
You're giving me a key. I don't know what to say. Nobody's ever done that for me.
Your spare key! I'm threading it on a string so I can never lose it.
A key to your home. That's a big thing, {player}. I know it is. Thank you.
I'll keep it safe. And if you're ever away too long, I'll come and water the plant.
Right. If you're out when I come by, I'll wait inside. With the kettle on.
I'll only use it when it matters. Or when you've run out of food. Which matters.
It goes next to my own house key. Now I've two homes to look after.
This milk has started to have opinions. Still drinkable. Just.
The milk smells like it's thinking about becoming cheese.
Slightly sour milk. Good for the bones, maybe. Less good for the face you're making.
The milk has turned into yoghurt without asking anyone's permission.
This milk is no longer milk. It's a new and independent thing. Leave it in peace.
Pouring the milk makes a sound milk shouldn't make. Down the sink it goes.
The onigiri's gone a little hard. Crunchy rice is still rice.
Yesterday's onigiri. The seaweed has given up, but the rice soldiers on.
This rice ball could double as a training weight. Chew slowly.
This onigiri has turned to stone. You could practise on the target board with it.
The onigiri clonks on the plate. Maybe the sparrows will want it.
That rice ball is a doorstop now. A small, sad doorstop.
The dango's gone chewy. Very chewy. Your jaw is getting a workout.
Stale dango. The sauce has set like varnish, but it's still sweet.
Day-old dango tastes a little like patience.
The dango could bounce now. Go on, try it. ...It does bounce.
These dango are so hard they clack together like beads on a string.
Old dango, stiff as the stick it's on. Your teeth would rather you didn't.
The bread's gone a bit dry. Toast it and nobody will ever know.
Crusty bread. Crustier than anyone intended.
This bread crunches when you squeeze it. That's not usual.
The bread is hard enough to knock on. Someone might answer.
This loaf could be a training weapon. Not a good one.
The bread snaps instead of tearing. Crumble it for the birds on the balcony.
The fruit's gone soft and wrinkly. Sweeter for it, maybe.
A bit of a bruise on this one. Eat around it.
The mikan's skin is loose and baggy, as if it's wearing someone else's coat.
This fruit has gone so wrinkly it looks a hundred years old.
The fruit is very, very soft. It's had a long life. Let it rest.
This apple squashes if you so much as look at it. Time for a new one.
The cabbage is a bit floppy. Soup will hide it.
These carrots bend. Carrots shouldn't bend.
The greens have wilted. They look how you feel after laps round the training ground.
The carrots bend all the way round into circles now. Impressive. Not supper.
The cabbage has gone so limp it's lying down. Let it sleep.
These vegetables have given up entirely. Off to the compost with them, with thanks.
Leftovers from a few days back. Fine warmed up, though the flavour's gone a bit flat.
This stew tastes more like a memory of stew.
Day-old curry is better than fresh, people say. Third-day curry is a gamble.
The leftovers have been here so long they've forgotten what they were.
That home cooking is past saving. Better make a fresh pot.
Whatever this was, it was delicious once. Farewell, supper.
The bento's rice is going hard at the edges. The pickles are fine, at least.
Yesterday's bento. The egg's gone a little rubbery, but it'll do.
A tired bento. Everything's still in its little section, holding on bravely.
That bento has sat in the cupboard so long it belongs in a museum.
Even the pickles in this bento look disappointed.
That bento box needs a wash and a fresh start, in that order.
A bit past its best, this. Still food, though.
That's gone a little stale. It shouldn't have sat in the cupboard so long.
Not fresh, not ruined. Somewhere in between, like a grey afternoon.
That's been in the cupboard so long it's practically a lodger.
Very stale. If it had a name, it would be "Too Late".
Time to clear out the cupboard. Some of this is older than your kunai pouch.
You kept the {gift}! And it's on the shelf, where people can see it.
Is that my {gift}? Up there with the good things? I'm a bit proud, actually.
Don't think I missed the {gift}. I was worried it would end up at the back of a drawer.
The {gift} looks better here than it ever did in the shop window.
Every time I visit I'm going to check the {gift} is still there. Just so you know.
My {gift}, on show! I nearly bought a second one to keep it company.
You gave the {gift} pride of place. Come here, I'm hugging you, no arguments.
That's... the {gift}. You kept it out. I didn't think... thank you.
The {gift}, front and centre. Naturally. I do choose well.
Hey, the {gift}! Front row! Did you dust it before I came, or is it always that shiny?
You kept the {gift}, and kept it clean. Good. Things given should be looked after.
The {gift}. ...Hm. Good spot for it.
Our class photo! Look at us, squinting into the sun on the Academy steps.
Someone in the back row is pulling a face. I know who. I'm not telling.
You hung the class photo! My copy is still rolled up under the bed.
Everyone's standing so stiff. We were told not to move and took it far too seriously.
That's me blinking. I blinked on purpose. It's art, {player}.
The frame's a hair crooked. There. Now the whole class is level.
Everyone looks so small in this. It wasn't even that long ago.
Whose hand is that, poking in at the corner? It's bothered me since the day it was taken.
Look at that fist in the air! Best class the Academy ever had, I said so then and I say so now!
Funny. A photo makes a class look settled, as if we already knew each other back then.
Graduation day. Your headband's on a little crooked in this. It suits you.
I still remember how heavy the headband felt that morning. Look at those faces.
You framed it! Good. That day was worth a nail in the wall.
Terrified and thrilled at once, every one of us. That's graduation, I suppose.
Everyone in that photo earned the headband. Don't let anyone forget it.
Look at you, all shining forehead and big grin. I could cry all over again.
Straight backs, all of us. Shame about the scuffed sandals. Polish them next time.
I nearly didn't stand in the picture. I'm glad I did. ...I'm on the end, there.
The light's all gold in this. Like the whole day had been dipped in honey.
That was the day we promised to look out for each other. I meant it. I still do.
The squad photo, from the very first day. Before any of us knew what we were in for.
Everyone in this one is trying so hard to look like a proper team. It's sweet.
You hung the squad photo where you see it from the door. Good place for it.
The day the squad was made. Doesn't it feel longer ago than it is?
Look at that! The team that's going to turn the Leaf upside down! Or help it. Mostly help it.
First day. Sloppy stances, the lot of us. We've come a long way since.
Bet you can't guess who stepped on whose foot right before it was taken.
Every face in that frame has come home from every mission so far. Let's keep it that way.
Hm. We look young.
I wish it showed what came after. The roads, the missions. That's the real picture.
Our first C-rank! Look at the mud on everyone's sandals.
That's the road out past the gate. I can almost smell the campfire.
Nobody in this photo had slept properly in two days. You can tell.
You put the road photo up! Every time I see it I want to pack a bag.
Furthest past the wall any of us had ever been. I'd go back tomorrow.
Look at the size of that pack. Half of what was in it never came out. Lesson learned.
The sky behind us looks painted on. It really was that blue, wasn't it?
I counted heads every morning on that road. All present. Good.
Someone's got a leaf stuck in their hair in this. It's you. It was always you.
A real mission, done properly, start to finish. That's worth a frame.
The festival photo! Look at all the lanterns behind us.
That was the night the goldfish game nearly beat us. Look at the little bags in our hands.
Everyone's got sauce somewhere in this one. Festival rules.
I love this one. You can see the first fireworks going up over the Hokage Rock.
Look, I'm wearing the fox mask on the back of my head. The height of fashion.
Everyone's smiling. Even the ones who never smile. What a night that was.
All those lanterns look like a river of tiny suns running behind us.
Who actually took this, in the end? I've asked everyone and they all say someone else.
I'm half behind the lantern pole. I didn't mean to be. ...I like it anyway.
Loudest night of the year, and I was the loudest thing in it!
The Chunin Exams. A week I'll never forget, whatever the board said at the end.
We all look so tired in this. Tired, and somehow proud.
You hung this one. Good. Whatever happened in that arena, we came out of it together.
Bandages, bruises and grins. The whole exam fits in one picture.
We stood in front of the whole village that week. Look how straight we're standing still.
Every bruise in that picture taught somebody something. Remember what yours taught you.
I remember holding my breath for you in the stands. Look, you can see the bandage on your arm.
I can still hear the crowd! I swear the whole stadium was shaking!
Odd, how a week can feel like a year. That photo has the whole year in it.
Everyone walked out of that arena on their own feet. That's what I see when I look at this.
Don't apologise for the mess. It looks like somebody actually lives here.
Shove the scrolls over, I'll sit on the floor. I like it like this.
Messy? This is nothing. You should see my room.
A few dishes never hurt anybody. Sit down, I didn't come to inspect.
Is the laundry pile a fort? Can I be in the fort?
Looks like camp after a long day on the road. Feels like home to me.
All those things lying about, it's like the room is halfway through telling a story.
Leave it, leave it. You've had a long week. The dishes will still be there tomorrow.
Mess. Don't care. Where's the cushion?
Who cares about dishes! Tidying's for people with nothing better to do!
How many cups is that on the windowsill? No, don't tell me. I'll count.
I'm not saying anything. I'm just going to stand here and look at the sink.
Your floor is under there somewhere. I've seen it. Once.
I'll make you a deal: I'll sit down when I can see the cushion.
Bowls, three. Cups, five. Socks, unpaired. I'm only noting it. For now.
A shinobi's kit is only as tidy as a shinobi's room. Wash those bowls before you sleep.
I'd never let my room look like this. Then again, I'd never let anyone see it if I did.
One quick go at the sink and you'd sleep better. A few seconds. I'll time you.
Right, sleeves up, I'm doing the dishes while we talk. Don't argue, it's no trouble.
You can't see the floor, and you'll trip in the dark. Clear a path to the door, at least.
Long days lately? The flat looks like it's had them too.
Mind the bowls by the door. I nearly went over on one.
There's a sock on the lamp. I'm choosing not to ask.
It looks like the place has been fighting back this week.
How does a chopstick end up on top of the cupboard? Genuinely, how?
I'll just... sit here. On this bit. That's clear. It's fine.
A busy room usually means a busy head. Everything all right, {player}?
Want a hand with this before I go? Two of us, it's done in no time.
I'm going to guess what you ate this week from the bowls alone. Ramen. Ramen. Ramen?
It's cosy, in its way. A little crowded with dishes, that's all.
One, two, three... {player}, the ramen cups are forming a tower.
That's a lot of instant ramen. Have you eaten anything green this week?
The cups are stacked so neatly, they're almost a piece of furniture.
I can tell which flavour you like best. It's that one. All of those are that one.
That settles it. I'm cooking for you next time, and there'll be vegetables in it.
Look at that stack! That's dedication! I respect it!
Six empty cups, all the same flavour. You could at least vary the order.
If you get to ten, we light a candle on top and call it a shrine.
You can't train on cup noodles alone. Rice. Fish. Greens. I'll be asking.
Do you rinse them first, or just stack them? Does the tower ever fall over in the night?
Swept, dusted, dishes away. I'm impressed, {player}. Honestly.
Look at this. Everything has a place and everything's in it.
Did you clean before I came, or is it always like this? Either way, well done.
Even the sandals by the door are lined up. You're showing off now.
Scrolls in order, bowls stacked by size. ...By size! Oh, I could live here.
Clean. Orderly. Keep it like this and your kit will follow.
This is how a room should look. I'm glad one of my friends understands.
Tidy rooms waste less. Nothing lost, nothing bought twice. Smart.
It's so fresh in here! Mind you don't wear yourself out keeping it this nice.
Clear floor, clear path to the door. Good. That's a safe room.
A Leaf banner and a paper lamp. It feels like the village lives in here with you.
Tatami, a low table, a proper cushion. This is a real Leaf room.
That folding screen is lovely. Simple things done well.
The paper lamp makes the whole room glow. I could sit under it all night.
It's just like the old houses by the river. Warm wood, warm light. I feel at home already.
Good, plain Leaf things. They'll last. This is a room you can rely on.
I love the scroll shelf. All your things resting there, quietly.
A Leaf banner in a Leaf flat. Somehow it reads as a promise more than a decoration.
The village crest on your wall. Wear it like that on the outside too.
The tatami's laid the proper way, edges never meeting in a cross. Someone's done this right.
A noren in your doorway! It's like walking into Ichiraku.
Is that an Ichiraku stool? Did they let you have it, or... no, don't tell me.
The ramen poster, the bowl shelf. You've built a little ramen stand in here.
All you need now is the smell of pork broth and I'd never leave.
A ramen corner! This is the best flat in the whole village and I won't hear otherwise!
Two bowls, extra egg, please. What? There's a noren. It's a restaurant now.
A home with a ramen shelf is a home where nobody goes hungry. I approve completely.
Every stand on the road out of the Leaf had a curtain like that. Takes me right back.
A whole set of furniture in honour of noodles. ...It is a very good set, I'll give you that.
Where did you find a poster like that? Did the stand give it you? Does it come in other flavours?
The wind chime! I heard it from the stairs.
A bench on the balcony. Can we sit out there? Just for a minute?
The planter's coming on. Your balcony is turning into a little garden.
Is that a bonsai? It's so small and so serious. I love it.
The chime and the plants and the breeze. It's like the balcony is breathing.
From your bench the rooftops look like waves. We could sail off over them.
Your balcony is... really nice. Quiet. Could I sit out there for a bit?
Good view. Good bench. I'll be out there.
Washing on the line and a bonsai beside it. The everyday and the patient, side by side.
You can see right over to the gate from here! Look, the road's just there!
A target board in your flat! Do the neighbours mind the thunk?
You've got a proper training corner. No excuses for skipping practice now.
That dummy's taken some hits. Good.
A meditation mat beside a weapon rack. Rest and steel in one corner. I like the balance.
Now this is a shinobi's flat. Show me what you can do on that board.
A weapon rack is only worth anything if the weapons on it are oiled. Are they?
Spar with me! Right now! You've got a dummy, I've got energy, let's go!
Good. The more you practise at home, the safer you'll be out there.
The target board is a finger too high for your reach. Lower it and your grouping will tighten.
I bet I can hit the middle of that board from your doorway. Bet me. Go on.
A proper tea set! Shall I pour, or would you like to?
The hanging scroll and the flowers in the vase. It's very calm in this corner.
Two zabuton by the tea table. You were expecting company.
This corner smells faintly of green tea. It's lovely.
A tea corner is a place to think slowly. Everyone should have one, and few people do.
The cups are set straight and the scroll hangs true. Good. Tea is a discipline too.
Shall we just sit here a while? We don't even need to talk.
The ikebana is lovely. One stem is leaning, may I? ...There. Perfect.
A good tea set keeps you off the tea house bill. Clever, and pleasant with it.
I like your tea corner. It's quiet. ...Can I sit on that cushion?
Lanterns strung up inside! It's festival night every night in here.
Is that a goldfish from the festival? Look at it go!
A festival drum. Please tell me you play it. Badly. Loudly.
The masks on the wall keep watching me. In a friendly way.
Mask on! Fans out! We're having a festival right here, right now!
Which stall did that fox mask come from? The one by the shrine steps? I've wanted one for ages.
With the lanterns lit it's like the whole festival came home with you and never left.
A goldfish! Have you named it? Are you feeding it enough? Let me see it eat.
A drum! Give me the sticks! The neighbours love a bit of rhythm, I'm sure of it!
The paper fans are pretty. I've got one like the blue one, at home.
Those are my clan's colours on your wall. You didn't have to. ...I'm really glad you did.
A banner in our colours, in your flat. You'd be welcome at our table any day, you know.
That lantern is in our clan's colours. My family would be pleased to see it. I'm pleased to see it.
You picked our colours. Nobody has to be born into a clan to be a friend of one.
Our colours, hung properly and in good light. You've done our clan justice. I won't forget it.
Our banner! Oh, you're coming to dinner at ours, I don't care what you say.
Our colours. ...Thank you. Means more than I'll say.
You hung our banner with care. My elders would approve. So do I.
Look at you, more in our colours than half my cousins! I'm telling them. They'll be furious.
Those are my colours. Seeing them here feels like you've saved me a seat.
What is all this? A cracked bell, a stone with a face, half a kite... I love it.
Your shelf of odd things grows every time I come. Where does it all come from?
Is that a single straw sandal? Where's the other one? Don't tell me, I like the mystery.
None of this is useful at all, is it? That's what makes it wonderful.
A bent spoon, a bottle with a bead inside and a painted pebble. Every one has a story, I bet.
Wait, wait. Where did you find the bottle with the bead in? How did the bead get in?
You could sell the lot for about four ryo. ...Don't. Somehow it's worth more on the shelf.
A museum of tiny, useless treasures. I could make up a legend for every one.
If you sorted them by size, or colour, or age... no? Fine. They're charming as they are.
I'm bringing you something for the collection next time. Something truly pointless.
Your plant is flowering! You've been looking after it.
Look at those blossoms. The season got into your flat.
It's in flower! Mine never does that. What's your secret?
Those flowers make the whole room smell green and sweet.
Hello, little one. You're doing so well.
The petals are the colour of the sky just before the lanterns come on.
It flowered... that's lovely. You must water it a lot. ...Could I have a seed, sometime?
How long did it take to bloom? Does it flower every year? Does it smell different at night?
A flowering plant in a home means someone's being looked after properly. Including you, I hope.
Healthy roots, good light. You've put that pot in exactly the right window.
{pet:player}! Come here, come here. Who's a good one?
Hello, {pet:player}. Did you keep the flat safe while {player} was out?
{pet:player} remembers me! Look, straight to my feet.
A pet makes a place feel lived in. {pet:player} looks very much at home.
Shh, {pet:player} is sleeping. Let's be quiet. Look how peaceful.
{pet:player}, catch! ...Or don't. That's also a choice.
{pet:player} came straight to me. ...Animals are easier than people, sometimes.
Fed, brushed and clear-eyed. {pet:player} is well kept. Good.
Does {pet:player} sleep on the bed or at the foot of it? What does {pet:player} do all day while you're out?
{pet:player}. ...Hey.
It's a bit bare, isn't it? We'll find you a cushion or two.
A futon, a table and a cupboard. That's how everyone starts out.
You could use a lamp. And a rug. And maybe a second cup, for guests.
It echoes a little in here. It just needs some of you in it.
Plain and clean. There's room here for all the things you haven't found yet.
I like the window. That's a good start. The rest will come.
You need a cushion. Two. And a blanket for winter. I'm making a list, and you're not stopping me.
The furniture shop has a floor cushion going cheap. Start there, then a lamp. One thing at a time.
An empty room is like a fresh scroll. Think of everything you could paint on it.
Bare is fine. Bare is honest. Keep it clean and fill it slowly.
So much floor! We could have a race from the door to the window.
It's... quiet in here. I could bring you something. If you wanted.
A few things of your own now. It's starting to look like you.
